summary: A 40-ft steel tower built in 2017 in Big Pocono State Park, replacing a 1921 21-ft Aermotor LS 40 that was moved to Grey Towers for restoration.

facts.design: 40 ft steel tower (2017), maker not named; predecessor was a 21 ft Aermotor LS 40 steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab (1921)

events.note: 21 ft steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab erected on Big Pocono; Pike County Courier gives 1919 and 35 ft, and a 1921 newspaper expected 20 ft
Old 21 ft tower disassembled as part of Pennsylvania's fire tower network upgrade
40 ft steel replacement tower built on the site as part of the upgrade
Old tower moved to Grey Towers National Historic Site, the former home of Gifford Pinchot
New tower registered on the National Historic Lookout Register January 15, 2018 as US 1264
Grey Towers project reassembled the old tower's restored cab in summer 2019; the register had expected re-erection in 2018 and the project planned placement in 2021

corrections.proposed: 2017 replaced (40 ft tower built in 2017); 2017 removed (21 ft predecessor built 1921)
corrections.why: The NHLR entry and the Forest Lookouts history both date the replacement tower to 2017. 2018 is the NHLR registration date, not the construction date.

corrections.proposed: 40 ft steel tower (2017), maker not named; predecessor 21 ft Aermotor LS 40 steel tower with 7 x 7 ft cab (1921)
corrections.why: The Aermotor Model LS 40 description applies to the 21 ft predecessor per Grey Towers. The NHLR entry for the 40 ft tower names no manufacturer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR 1921 entry and the Forest Lookouts history give 1921, while the Pike County Courier says the tower was first installed in 1919. The story uses 1921 and notes the disagreement.

The NHLR entries and Grey Towers give 21 ft, a 1921 newspaper expected 20 ft, and the Pike County Courier describes a 35 ft tower. The story uses 21 ft from the register and Grey Towers and reports the other figures.

The NHLR 1921 entry says the old tower will be re-erected in 2018. Grey Towers says the cab was reassembled in 2019 and plans placement in 2021. The story reports both and says the dates do not line up.

sources.title: Big Pocono fire tower migrates to Grey Towers

notes_for_editor: The brief's Aermotor design is supported only for the 1921 predecessor, so the record should not attribute it to the 2017 tower. Predecessor date and height disagree across the NHLR, the Forest Lookouts history, the 1921 newspaper item and the Pike County Courier, and the story reports those disagreements. Re-erection timing disagrees too (NHLR 2018 vs Grey Towers 2019 reassembly and 2021 plan). Access for the 2017 tower is not established: the NHLR entry has no visit information, and no state park or DCNR visit rules were read, so the access and visit keys are left out rather than guessed. Staffing history was not found in these sources. No photos were added because no licensed image URL was confirmed. The NHLR 1921 entry's photo credits were not used. Searches surfaced a Wildfire Today article and a PA Environment Digest piece on the 16-tower replacement program, but those were not read, so they are not cited. Story is about 330 words.
